title: Find My Location: Coordinates and Address
description: Drop a pin where you are with Find My Location — your coordinates and address, computed in your browser and not stored. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, one click on a country walk turns 'somewhere past the second gate' into coordinates you can read to a friend, a taxi or a rescue service.
quick_answer: Find My Location uses your device's positioning to drop a pin where you are and shows your coordinates and address. Press the button, allow access, and read the result — the position is computed for this page in your browser, and the address comes from a public reverse geocoder.

faq: No. The position is obtained for this page's display; MapBench does not store your browser location. The address lookup sends the coordinates to a public reverse geocoder for that one answer.
Move to open sky, give it a few seconds, and check the accuracy figure. Tall buildings and indoors scatter fixes; a second reading outdoors usually settles streets away from the first.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
The page's purpose is your location, so it needs the permission — decline it and nothing is read. Other tools here work from typed places instead.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
The address comes from open geocoding data; another service's record can name the same street corner differently.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Your browser is enforcing your earlier choice. Re-allow location for this site in the browser's settings if you want the pin.
In sparse-data country the reverse geocoder may return little. The coordinates remain exact and usable everywhere else on this site.
Which system are the coordinates in?
WGS84 latitude/longitude — the system GPS and web maps share.
